title: Soveraeign Node Identity
description: Who a node is, and which seat settles for it. One record per node a local node knows about: itself, and every peer it has admitted. Identity only. This contract deliberately cannot express a grant, a capability, a scope, or any other authority, so a peer's identity record can never be mistaken for permission inside the node that holds it (decisions/0039).

node_id.description: Opaque local identifier. decisions/0039 takes the default that no DNS name, key, or discovery address is chosen in this phase; a node_id resolves to a peer only through a crossing a local seat admitted.

relation.description: SELF is the node holding this registry. PEER is another sovereign node this one has admitted. Exactly one SELF is a registry rule, not a record rule; scripts/sovkernel/node_identity.py checks it.

root_seat.description: The seat that settles for this node. For SELF it must be a root-type seat in the local topology. For PEER it names the peer's own root seat, which must NOT appear in the local topology: identity travels across a crossing, authority does not.

known_since.description: When this node learned of the peer. Null for SELF, which did not learn of itself.

admitted_by.description: The local seat that admitted this peer. Null for SELF. A peer that no local seat admitted is not in the registry at all.
